newsitem.title: CHINA: China says opposed to U.S. attack threat on Iraq.
newsitem.headline: China says opposed to U.S. attack threat on Iraq.

text.p: China said on Friday that it strongly opposed apparent U.S plans for an attack on Iraq and urged restraint, saying all such problems should be resolved in line with United Nations resolution.
"The Chinese government expresses its concern and unease over the recent aggravation of the situation in the Gulf," Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang said in a statement.
China "appeals to those concerned to adopt an attitude of restraint to prevent the further escalation of the tense situation in the region", he said.
U.S. ships and assault planes closed in on Iraq on Friday in preparation for a possible new military strike to end President Saddam Hussein's defiance of allied patrols of Iraqi air space.
The carrier Enterpise and its task force was sailing from the Adriatic to the Gulf to join the carrier Carl Vinson.
"The U.S. threat to use new military strikes against Iraq will only further aggravate tension in the Gulf region," Shen said. "We express our strong opposition."
The problems in the Gulf should be resolved by reasonable political means and on the basis of U.N. resolutions, he said.
This will allow "the quick return of peace and stability in the Gulf region," he said.

U.S.-Iraqi tensions began rising last week when U.S. planes and ships fired 44 cruise missiles at southern Iraqi air defences in retaliation for the Iraqi military's move against a Kurdish faction in the north of the country.
But U.S. officials said they detected no movement of Iraqi forces south toward Kuwait.
